newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk unit 96 nickel output 100,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk unit 96 nickel output 100,000 T.

text.p: Russia's Norilsk Nickel combine, the flagship plant of the Norilsk metals group, produced 100,000 tonnes of nickel in 1996 and forecast flat 1997 output.

A senior official at the Norilsk mining and enriching complex who declined to be identified said in a telephone interview that cobalt output last year was 1,500 tonnes and that it would be flat in 1997.
"We produced what we planned. Last year can be seen as a year of stabilisation," he said. He had no information on copper production.
The combine accounts for more than half of RAO Norilsky Nikel's 0#NKEL.RUO nickel production and for the bulk of its cobalt output.

The plant, based in the Arctic town of Norilsk, in 1995 produced about 93,800 tonnes of nickel, over 1,500 tonnes of cobalt and nearly 266,000 tonnes of copper, according to company data from December 1996.
The Norilsk group has said it expects its total 1996 nickel output to rise three percent and refined copper output six percent on 1995 levels.

Norilsk spokesman Sergei Vetchinin said in Moscow that the company was not prepared to release overall production figures or forecasts and that 1996 had been a financially difficult year for the troubled metals group.
The group's 1995 nickel output was 180,100 tonnes while refined copper output was 338,700 tonnes.

Russia is the world's largest miner of nickel ore and concentrate and Norilsk is the world's second largest refined nickel producer. The Norilsk group accounts for about 85 percent of Russian nickel output.
